mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team A's shots FOR is elevated relative to its own long-run mean (recent-5 vs ALL_PRIOR divergence) while corner_kicks FOR is simultaneously depressed relative to its own long-run mean. Measure whether shots_on_target FOR rises or falls in this joint state compared to the baseline where both observables move together.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When shot volume rises but corner production falls simultaneously, shots-on-target rate rises relative to the baseline where both observables are at their long-run levels — suggesting a more direct, central attacking mode rather than wide/set-piece-driven pressure.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot volume has risen sharply in recent matches while its conversion efficiency (shots-on-target rate) has also improved, but its corner-kick production has simultaneously declined. The joint relationship between shot volume, shots-on-target, and corner-kick production — specifically whether a team generating more shots but fewer corners is operating in a qualitatively different attacking mode — is worth measuring across historical match observations.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint conditioning on two distinct observables (shots and corner_kicks) simultaneously diverging from their own baselines in opposite directions, then measuring a third observable (shots_on_target). No single-observable mirror or single-band split covers this three-variable joint relationship.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where a team's shots_on_target FOR (recent-5) diverges upward from its ALL_PRIOR mean while shots_on_target AGAINST (recent-5) diverges downward from its ALL_PRIOR mean. Measure whether possession FOR is also elevated in this joint state, or whether the asymmetric shots-on-target pattern occurs independently of possession share.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When shots_on_target FOR rises and shots_on_target AGAINST falls simultaneously, possession FOR rises with this joint state — but the relationship saturates or reverses when possession is already near or above 50%, suggesting diminishing returns to possession-driven shot suppression.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shots-on-target FOR has surged in recent matches (6.0 vs 3.971 long-run) while its shots_on_target AGAINST has dropped (2.8 vs 3.956 long-run), creating an asymmetric divergence across the two sides of the same observable. The joint relationship between a team's own shots-on-target production trend and the shots-on-target it concedes — specifically whether these two dimensions move independently or co-vary — is worth measuring to understand whether recent form reflects genuine two-way improvement or a sample artifact.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves an asymmetric joint relationship across two distinct perspectives (FOR vs AGAINST) of the same observable, further conditioned on a second observable (possession). It cannot be reduced to a single observable's own-vs-allowed mirror or a single coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on match-level observations where the attacking team's offsides FOR is elevated (above its own long-run mean) while the defending team's offsides AGAINST is simultaneously low (below its own long-run mean). Measure whether corner_kicks FOR and shots FOR are suppressed in this joint state relative to matches where both offside rates are near their respective means.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When an attacking team's offside rate is high and the defending team's offside-concession rate is low simultaneously, the attacking team's corner_kicks and shots are suppressed — indicating that a high-line, well-organized defense neutralizes forward runs and reduces attacking volume.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A concedes substantially more offsides than it generates (2.264 against vs 1.708 for, ALL_PRIOR), while Team B generates more offsides than it concedes (1.926 for vs 0.926 against). The joint relationship between one team's offside-generation tendency and the opponent's offside-concession tendency — specifically whether high offside-generation by one side against a low-offside-conceding opponent suppresses corner and shot production — is worth measuring as a two-observable, two-team interaction.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (offsides FOR for one team, offsides AGAINST for the opponent) from two different teams simultaneously, then measuring a third observable. This is a two-team, two-observable interaction not reducible to any single-observable mirror or single-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where a team's fouls FOR (full match) is elevated above its own long-run mean. Within those matches, measure whether cards_2h FOR is disproportionately elevated relative to yellow_cards FOR (full match), testing whether foul-heavy teams accumulate cards non-linearly in the second half versus the first half.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's full-match foul rate is elevated above its long-run mean, its second-half card accumulation rises disproportionately relative to its full-match yellow card rate — suggesting a threshold or acceleration effect where foul accumulation in the first half leads to heightened card risk in the second half.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A generates substantially more cards in the second half than it concedes (1.603 FOR vs 1.123 AGAINST, cards_2h), while Team B's second-half card rates are nearly symmetric (1.324 FOR vs 1.397 AGAINST). The joint relationship between a team's second-half foul rate and its second-half card accumulation — specifically whether elevated foul production in the full match predicts asymmetric second-half card accumulation — is worth measuring as a within-match state interaction across two observables.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a within-match state split (second half vs full match) jointly conditioned on a second distinct observable (fouls), testing a non-linear threshold relationship. It is not reducible to a single observable's half-level split alone or a single coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where a team's second-half corner_kicks FOR exceeds its first-half corner_kicks FOR by more than its long-run half-differential. Measure whether goals FOR in the second half are also elevated relative to the first half in those same matches, versus matches where the corner-kick half-differential is near zero or reversed.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's second-half corner production exceeds its first-half corner production by more than its historical norm, its second-half goal production also rises relative to its first-half goal production — suggesting that corner-kick momentum within a match is a leading indicator of second-half scoring uplift.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner-kick production is split across halves (2.169 first half vs 2.815 second half FOR, ALL_PRIOR), and its goals are similarly back-loaded (0.589 first half vs 0.877 second half FOR). Team B shows a similar half-level pattern for goals (0.574 first half vs 0.838 second half FOR). The joint relationship between a team's corner-kick half-level distribution and its goal-scoring half-level distribution — specifically whether teams that generate disproportionately more corners in the second half also score disproportionately more goals in the second half — is worth measuring as a two-observable, within-match sequencing interaction.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on the within-match half-level differential of one observable (corner_kicks) to predict the within-match half-level differential of a second distinct observable (goals). It involves two observables and a within-match sequencing structure, not reducible to any single-observable half split or single-band conditioning.
